BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (buyer-side, privileged and confidential)
**Basis:** Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter, reviewed against the Wattlebridge playbook.
**Note:** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. It is now 5 November 2026, so the open items below (Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006, Ironquay, bonuses) need refreshed facts before we rely on them either way.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% is our conditional fallback, available only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost for this draft. No such authority exists, and a number matching our fallback does not mean it is cleared.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, and only the excess over the basket is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restate the playbook figures and tipping mechanism.**
- **Reason:** The seller's terms are five times our thresholds, and the deductible structure permanently removes the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims only, with separate periods for other categories.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.**
- **Reason:** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The default wording would quietly shorten the Title, Tax, indemnity and fraud periods.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. Exposing them to a 20% cap would leave about 80% of the price unprotected if title fails.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5). There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out. This is non-negotiable.**
- **Reason:** The "any nature" wording would arguably shield seller fraud. The playbook says no one may waive this protection.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, against identified warranties.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete DL 1.1–1.2 as general disclosures.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure moves all diligence risk to us and hollows out the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier should rest on named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete cl 8.3.**
- **Reason:** As drafted, it would defeat even the specific indemnities for issues we disclosed and priced, such as Ironquay.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The DL confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent as a Completion condition, plus evidence that its cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m). Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a customer this material.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with the release to follow Completion. The DL confirms the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** The deal is debt-free and our playbook bars post-completion release. That could only be considered with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which is offered. The AUD 3.2m figure also needs a current payout statement.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, either as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the silent exclusion.**
- **Reason:** These are Completion-triggered company liabilities. If they are not itemised or funded, the cost falls on us after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and described as "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity covering ownership, transfer and assignment of the Ironquay Project Materials and third-party claims, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted. Broaden it and require a confirmatory assignment.**
- **Reason:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes IP transfer conditional on cleared payment, and no receipt or assignment exists. The AUD 180,000 open amount (DD-010) is unverified either way, so the indemnity cannot be tied to that figure alone.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** Preservation of logs, a proper investigation, ongoing updates through Completion, and appropriate warranty or indemnity coverage.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Require investigation and update covenants.**
- **Reason:** The DL itself says access, scope and any notification duty are unestablished (about 1,240 records). We should assume neither a confirmed breach nor its absence, and make no numeric demand.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course (reading DD-008 with DD-011).
- **Recommendation:** **Hold. Request facts and do not concede the ordinary-course label.**
- **Reason:** The DL does not establish their nature, and the playbook also bars us from treating them automatically as Debt or a price deduction.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applies to all Claims", limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature", and Title, Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate Title, Tax, IP, payment-obligation and covenant regimes, with no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete the catch-all language and add an express hierarchy clause.**
- **Reason:** These sweeping provisions would collapse every protected category into the 20%, 18-month, AUD 250,000 deductible regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as ASIC searches, PPSR searches, issue and transfer records, board approvals and constitution checks.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as sufficient.**
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal seller-supplied source, and the DL (item 10) concedes no independent verification has been done.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as open and negotiated separately.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation.**
- **Reason:** These terms are open under our playbook. Calling them settled would import the general limits by assertion. We are not assuming unlimited liability or any agreed resolution.

---

### Overall
The seller's draft departs from our playbook on all 16 points. The most serious problems are structural:
- the catch-all limitation language (N-003, N-005, N-014);
- the missing fraud carve-out (N-005);
- Title being folded into the general regime (N-004, N-015);
- the data-room disclosure combined with the buyer-knowledge bar (N-006, N-007).

Together these would neutralise most buyer protections. The cover letter's description of the package as "fair and balanced" is an assertion and carries no weight.

Nothing in the draft constitutes authority to use any fallback. Amelia Frost should be told the seller is anchoring on our fallback numbers (20%, 18 months). That does not trigger approval; any move to those fallbacks still needs her written authority identifying this draft.
